newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Nemtsov to chair Russia Gazprom committee.
newsitem.headline: Nemtsov to chair Russia Gazprom committee.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin gave young government officials a new weapon to reform natural gas monopoly Gazprom by creating a committee to control the government's stake in Gazprom on Tuesday.

But the decree said an agreement should be offered to the chairman of Gazprom, Rem Vyakhirev, for management control of 35 percent of the company owned by the government, the presidential press service said.
The government has a total 40 percent stake in Gazprom.
Yeltsin named First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, generally charged with reforming the natural monopolies which have no competitors, to head the committee.
Nemtsov, quoted by Interfax news agency, said he spoke with Vyakhirev on Tuesday and would discuss the trust agreement on the 35 percent stake on Wednesday.

The committee is stacked with reformers including the new economy minister, heads of the State Tax Service and anti-monopoly committee and representatives of the pro-reform Federal Energy Commission and Federal Property Fund.
The decree also called for regulation on non-resident ownership of Gazprom, but gave no details.
